svg.text: HSM parallel regions — where does each action's data go?
The kernel really does run several leaf states per tick. The storage addressing does not know that.
THE KERNEL — genuinely concurrent
[FieldOffset(16)] fixed ushort ActiveLeafIds[4]; // max 4 regions
Region 0
leaf: WorkA
Activity → Patrol()
Region 1
leaf: WorkB
Activity → Patrol()
Region 2
leaf: WorkC
ProcessActivityPhase loops every region, then walks each leaf's
ancestor chain — all their Activity actions fire in ONE tick.
Per-region storage exists — but only for bookkeeping:
ActiveLeafIds[r] · TimerDeadlines[r] · HistorySlots[]
⇒ which state is active, and timers. ⛔ NOT action data.
Each state has 4 slots — Entry / Exit / Activity / Timer — all four dispatch identically.
THE ADDRESSING — knows nothing about regions
Slot key = hash(method name @ compile-time field offset)
CompoundKey = sym.Name + "@" + offset // FNV-1a → ushort
One shared table, keyed by that hash alone
Dictionary<ushort, IntPtr> ActionTable
ref Unsafe.AddByteOffset(ref bb.BehaviorParameters[0], (IntPtr)Offset)
⛔ no region index, no state id, no instance id anywhere in the path
⇒ TWO CONCURRENT REGIONS RUNNING THE SAME ACTION WRITE THE SAME BYTES
BrainBlackboard — ONE per entity
an ECS component, not an array
not indexed by state, region or slot
Blackboard1024 — same class of risk
its own doc admits the addressing is manual:
"each subsystem projects at a disjoint offset"
BTree does NOT have this problem
it provisions per-scope partition slots via
ResolveStatefulSlotKey — Node/Behavior/Entity
THE GUARDS EXIST — AND TWO OF THEM NEVER FIRE
Rule 8 · ConcurrentStatefulSubtree
"produces synthetic key collisions and race-write corruption"
Rule 8b · ConcurrentSharedScopeKey
"orthogonal regions race and corrupt the slot" — this is exactly it
Both are ERRORS. Both are correct. Both are unreachable.
Why they never fire
_isStatefulSubtree = isStatefulSubtree ?? (_ => false);
_sharedScopeKeys = sharedScopeKeys ?? (_ => Empty);
Both production call sites use the default ctor. The XML doc itself
says "Production should wire this" — so it is unfinished wiring,
not a dead rule. Only unit tests pass real resolvers.
